notes: Country determination: Germany (high certainty) - EU license plate 'L KD 3455' (L = Leipzig) 520x110 mm in photo 1, Gelbe-Tonne wheelie bins in photo 8, roller shutters, clinker/stucco facade, IBC tote, zinc downspouts. Calc profile DE.
Brick format: dark clinker, format ambiguous (DF course 62.5 vs Reichsformat ~78 mm); 75 mm course assumed at medium reliability, coursing chains down-weighted accordingly.
Entry door assumed 2110 mm; architecture suggests 1920s-1950s, so door-based scale treated as statistical per pre-1950 rule and cross-checked against coursing.
Yaw estimates: photo 1 ~8 deg, photo 6 ~10 deg, photo 8 ~15 deg; width chains anchored on near-frontal photo 3 (yaw <5 deg, correction <2% neglected, perspective_corrected=false).
Front slope carries an eyebrow (segmental-arch) dormer with a small guard railing in front of the window.
Back shed dormer and one left-side upper window are covered with white renovation sheeting; their dimensions are estimates of the underlying openings.
Firewood rack, rain barrels, hoses, bicycle and garden furniture treated as movable objects, not attachments.
Antenna/satellite hardware partially visible at photo 2 top-right corner: not assessable, omitted.
Raised ground floor at back (site slopes down toward garden); external metal garden stair and terrace are garden structures, not part of the building.
Facade corners sit inside the image frame with margin in photos 1 and 3: wide-angle corner-compression risk low there; close-ups 2, 4, 5, 9 are wide-angle/steep and used only locally.
Width/depth chains run at wall line (doors, windows, IBC), not at roof edge, so no soffit-depth subtraction was applied to footprint values (OVERHANG RULE).

warnings: total_width chains disagree by >8%: window-sum ~13200 mm vs vehicle-length-based ~8000 mm (vehicle chain weak: SUV stands in front of the facade plane and camera standoff distances are unknown); both kept per disagreement rule, width anchor confidence capped low.
total_width has only one robust horizontal chain (window group sum); brick stretcher coursing not countable across the facade at photo distance.
Ground line occluded on all front photos (fence, hedge, parked cars): eave/ridge heights assume the ground offset at the facade; height confidence capped medium-to-low per vertical anchor rule.
Photos 4 and 5 are steep upward wide-angle shots: verticals compressed, height chains from these photos capped low.
Clinker brick format ambiguous (DF 62.5 mm vs Reichsformat ~78 mm course); 75 mm assumed at medium reliability for all coursing chains.
Back ground floor partially occluded by party guests and vegetation in photo 6: back door D-4 is inferred from the external stair, openings on back GF may be undercounted.
Front-left corner of the facade is hidden by a tree in photos 1/3: a fourth downspout may exist there.
Shed dormer (AT-4) and left upper window (W-12) covered with renovation sheeting; dimensions estimated from the sheeted outlines.
Annex roof surfaces not visible: covering assumed membrane with estimated pitch per ATTACHMENT ROOF RULE.
Right annex (AT-8) seen in one oblique photo only; its orientation along the right wall and the placement of D-6 are uncertain.
Roof pitch estimated from oblique views only (~33 deg); no roof plan or frontal slope view available.
